name: Second Helpings
tagline: Recipes for weeknights and slow Sundays

els.text: Good food on a Tuesday night.
Weeknight suppers, weekend baking and the odd slow Sunday. Every recipe here is cooked in a small kitchen at least three times before it goes up.

els.alt: A cook stirring a red pot on the stove with a wooden spoon
Hands chopping fresh herbs on a wooden board

els.text: I’m Ines. I cook in a very small kitchen in Leeds.
No fancy kit, nothing you have to order online. If a recipe here needs a special pan, I will tell you what to use instead.
Follow along in any feed reader, or write to me with what you cooked.
I learned to cook from my grandmother, who never measured anything, and from a lot of library books, which measured everything. Second Helpings sits somewhere in between.
I test every recipe at least three times, on a normal oven, with supermarket ingredients. If something goes wrong when you make it, I want to hear about it.

els.alt: Hands feeding fresh pasta dough through a pasta machine

sections.heading: Tell me what you cooked
sections.text: Questions about a recipe, a swap that worked, or a photo of your plum cake. I read everything and answer most of it.

posts.title: Lemon chicken and potato bake
posts.content:
One dish, one oven, and a lemon doing most of the work. The potatoes soak up the juices underneath while the chicken skin crisps on top.

I make this on Mondays, when nobody wants to think about dinner.

Ingredients

  • 8 chicken thighs, skin on
  • 800g small potatoes, halved
  • 2 lemons, one sliced, one juiced
  • 4 cloves garlic, bashed
  • A few sprigs of thyme
  • 3 tbsp olive oil
  • Salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
  2. Toss the potatoes, garlic, lemon juice and half the oil in a large dish. Season well.
  3. Sit the chicken on top, skin side up, tuck the lemon slices and thyme around, and drizzle with the rest of the oil.
  4. Roast for 40 minutes, until the skin is golden and the potatoes are soft.
  5. Rest for five minutes and serve with something green.

Swap the thyme for oregano and add olives for the last 10 minutes.

posts.title: Ginger noodle soup with greens
posts.content:
This is what I cook when I have a cold, or when it is raining, or when it is Wednesday. A hot, clear broth, a lot of ginger and whatever greens are in the fridge.

Ingredients

  • 1 litre good stock
  • A thumb of ginger, sliced
  • 2 cloves garlic, sliced
  • 2 tbsp soy sauce
  • 1 tsp sesame oil
  • 2 nests of noodles
  • 2 handfuls of greens: pak choi, spinach or kale
  • 1 red chilli, sliced
  • 2 spring onions

Method

  1. Simmer the stock with the ginger and garlic for 10 minutes.
  2. Add the soy and sesame oil and taste. It should be salty and warm.
  3. Cook the noodles in the broth for 4 minutes, adding the greens for the last minute.
  4. Ladle into bowls and finish with chilli and spring onion.

posts.title: Plum and almond cake
posts.content:
September is plum month, and this is the cake for it. The plums sink into a soft almond sponge and turn jammy at the edges.

It keeps for three days, and is better on the second.

Ingredients

  • 175g soft butter
  • 175g caster sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 100g self-raising flour
  • 100g ground almonds
  • 1 tsp vanilla
  • 8 plums, halved and stoned
  • Icing sugar, to dust

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 23cm tin.
  2. Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
  3. Fold in the flour, almonds and vanilla. Spread into the tin.
  4. Press the plums in, cut side up.
  5. Bake for 50 to 55 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool, then dust with icing sugar.

posts.title: Tomato and butter bean stew
posts.content:
Cupboard food that does not taste like cupboard food. Two tins of beans, one of tomatoes, and enough garlic to make the house smell of it.

Ingredients

  • 3 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 onion, chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, sliced
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • 1 tin chopped tomatoes
  • 2 tins butter beans, drained
  • A handful of parsley
  • Thick toast, to serve

Method

  1. Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes.
  2. Add the garlic and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
  3. Tip in the tomatoes with half a tin of water and simmer for 10 minutes.
  4. Add the beans and cook for 5 minutes more, until thick. Season.
  5. Scatter with parsley and eat with toast.

posts.title: Brown butter banana bread
posts.content:
Browning the butter takes five extra minutes and makes this taste like a different cake. Use the blackest bananas you can find.

Ingredients

  • 115g butter
  • 3 very ripe bananas
  • 150g light brown sugar
  • 2 eggs
  • 1 tsp vanilla
  • 200g plain flour
  • 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda
  • A pinch of salt

Method

  1. Melt the butter in a pan and let it bubble until it smells nutty and turns golden brown. Cool slightly.
  2. Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) and line a loaf tin.
  3. Mash the bananas, then whisk in the butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
  4. Fold in the flour, soda and salt until just combined.
  5. Bake for 55 to 60 minutes. Cool in the tin for 15 minutes before turning out.

posts.title: Rosemary focaccia
posts.excerpt: 4 hours, mostly waiting · makes one tray
posts.content:
The easiest bread there is. No kneading, a lot of olive oil, and dimples you push in with your fingers, which is the best part.

Ingredients

  • 500g strong white flour
  • 7g fast-action yeast
  • 10g salt
  • 400ml warm water
  • 6 tbsp olive oil
  • Rosemary and flaky salt

Method

  1. Stir the flour, yeast, salt and water into a sticky dough. Cover and leave for 2 hours, until doubled.
  2. Pour half the oil into a deep tray, tip in the dough and stretch it to the corners. Leave for another hour.
  3. Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Dimple the dough all over with oily fingers, then add rosemary, salt and the rest of the oil.
  4. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, until deep gold. Cool for 10 minutes before cutting.

posts.title: Sunday roast chicken
posts.content:
Everyone should have one roast chicken they can make without a recipe. This is mine: butter under the skin, a lemon inside and a long rest at the end.

Ingredients

  • 1 chicken, about 1.8kg
  • 50g soft butter
  • 1 lemon
  • A head of garlic, halved
  • Thyme or tarragon
  • Salt and pepper

Method

  1. Take the chicken out of the fridge an hour before. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
  2. Push the butter under the skin of the breast and season well all over.
  3. Put the lemon, garlic and herbs inside the bird.
  4. Roast for 1 hour 20 minutes, until the juices run clear.
  5. Rest for 20 minutes, loosely covered. Make gravy from the tin while you wait.

posts.title: Fresh egg pasta by hand
posts.content:
Two ingredients and a rainy afternoon. You do not need a machine, though it helps. You do need a clear table and someone to talk to while you roll.

Ingredients

  • 400g 00 flour
  • 4 eggs
  • Semolina, for dusting

Method

  1. Make a well in the flour, crack in the eggs and work them together with a fork, then your hands.
  2. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and springy. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
  3. Roll out as thin as you can, in batches, dusting with semolina.
  4. Fold and cut into ribbons. Cook in well-salted boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes.

Toss with butter, lemon and parmesan the first time, so you can taste the pasta.
